content.user_title: Build Typed Error Handling with fp-ts
content.value_statement: Unchecked exceptions hide failure paths in TypeScript applications. This skill shows how to use fp-ts Either and TaskEither for explicit, composable error handling.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to replace try/catch with Either and TaskEither.
Shows how to wrap throwing functions and promises at boundaries.
Demonstrates chaining, mapping, folding, and widening error types.
Covers validation that accumulates multiple form errors.
Provides patterns for async API calls, retries, fallbacks, and partial success.
limitations: Does not install or configure fp-ts in a project.
Does not analyze a repository automatically.
Examples require adaptation to local domain types and libraries.
Assumes TypeScript and basic functional programming familiarity.

use_cases.title: Refactor Service Errors
use_cases.description: Turn hidden exceptions into typed return values that callers must handle.

use_cases.title: Validate Forms Fully
use_cases.description: Collect all field errors at once instead of stopping at the first failure.

use_cases.title: Design Async Failure Flows
use_cases.description: Model API calls, retries, fallbacks, and partial success with predictable types.

prompt_templates.title: Convert a Simple Function
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner refactor from exceptions to values.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this TypeScript function and show how to return an fp-ts Either instead of throwing. Explain the error and success branches.

prompt_templates.title: Model Validation Errors
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design fp-ts validation that returns every invalid field. Use clear domain error names and explain when to use error accumulation.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Async Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this async workflow into a TaskEither pipeline. Include boundary wrapping, typed errors, and final pattern matching.

prompt_templates.title: Design Domain Error Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an error-handling strategy for this TypeScript service using Either and TaskEither. Include domain errors, infrastructure errors, and caller behavior.

output_examples.input: A user lookup throws when the id is empty or the user is missing.
output_examples.output: The response describes an Either-based flow with InvalidId and NotFound errors, plus caller handling for each case.

output_examples.input: A form validator stops after the first invalid field.
output_examples.output: The response recommends validation accumulation and explains how email, password, and age errors can be returned together.

output_examples.input: An API workflow mixes nested try/catch blocks with promise chains.
output_examples.output: The response outlines a TaskEither pipeline with boundary wrapping, composed async steps, retry behavior, and final rendering logic.

best_practices: Keep error types specific enough for callers to choose behavior.
Convert throwing and Promise APIs at module boundaries.
Use validation applicatives when users need every input error.
anti_patterns: Wrapping every line in TaskEither without clearer failure semantics.
Collapsing all failures into unstructured strings too early.
Throwing inside a pipeline and bypassing typed error handling.

faq.question: What is Either in fp-ts?
faq.answer: Either represents a value that is either an error or a success. TypeScript can track both outcomes.

faq.question: What is TaskEither used for?
faq.answer: TaskEither models async work that can fail, such as API calls, database queries, and retries.

faq.question: Does this replace every exception?
faq.answer: No. It is best for expected failures that callers should handle explicitly.

faq.question: Can this collect multiple validation errors?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill explains applicative validation for collecting all field errors at once.

faq.question: Does the skill run commands or call services?
faq.answer: No. It is a Markdown guide with TypeScript examples and no executable project files.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: It fits TypeScript developers who want typed, composable error handling with fp-ts.
